steps.text: Place the green beans in a large saucepan or pot with one inch of water. You may place them in a steamer insert if you have one. Bring to a boil, cover and cook for 5 minutes, they should still be firm and bright green.
In a small bowl, stir together the soy sauce, balsamic vinegar and sugar; set aside.

Heat the sesame oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add garlic and cook until starting to brown. Add the green beans and stir to coat with the oil. Stir in the soy sauce mixture and simmer for a couple of minutes uncovered to reduce the sauce. Transfer the beans to a serving dish and pour the sauce over them.

raw_recipe.headline: Dad’s Pan-Fried Green Beans
raw_recipe.description: Once upon a time, Dad received a similar recipe with a bundle of fresh green beans. He made the recipe once and then lost the card. After many attempts to recreate that flavor, he declares that this, his own recipe, is even better!
raw_recipe.name: Dad’s Pan-Fried Green Beans

review.reviewBody:
Awesome! Just perfect. I don't bother with the vinegar because it's not necessary. I don't use one pound of GB's either--just a few handfuls. 

Run them under water, pinch off the ends and forget boiling them 1st. It's NOT necessary.

I add extra fresh crushed garlic to the pan and saute everything (covered) on a med-flame for 10-15 minutes so it's tender and flavorful! YUM!

This was terrific and went well with the honey-ginger grilled salmon from this site. I sauted the garlic in the sesame oil, when it began to brown I tossed in a bag of frozen whole green beans to begin to thaw and turned it off. This way the beans would not overcook while I finished the rest of the meal. When I pulled the salmon of the grill, I put the pan on high and finished them off. With only a 1/4 c. of liquid it was flavorful and not too saucy. Using frozen green beans mad this recipe super-fast and easy. Will make again and again. Thank you for sharing.

Very good recipe...I cut the balsamic in half, as suggested by other reviewers, and agree that it was probably better balanced. My adjustments: 1. I used olive oil (with a little butter added) instead of sesame oil, but had sesame seeds on hand so I threw in about a teaspoon (glad I did) 2. I added sliced onions to the garlic/butter/oil mixture and sauteed a little before adding the green beans. 3. I added a few drops of liquid smoke, but I don't think I really added enough to alter much 4. A little chopped bacon added at the end was delicious. All in all, I really enjoyed this, even though I made quite a few adjustments. Not sure if it would reheat well so serve it immediately. Will definitely make this again.
I used frozen green beans, the kind that microwave in the bag, which made this recipe very easy as well as delicious.

This was excellent. I skipped the parboiling of the beans and cooked them directly in the garlicky oil and the soy sauce mixture. Also, I decreased slightly the amount of soy sauce in the sauce mixture. The result was delicious, and I even used some of the cooking liquid as a dipping sauce for other items on the menu.

I never rate or comment on anything, ever, until I found this recipe. I've been looking for fun and healthy ways to dress up vegetables for myself and my boyfriend. Yes, he will eat anything, but this recipe gets him excited to eat veggies. I've been using this same recipe with various other greens besides green beans. The most common thing I use is frozen steam veggie bags I had purchased before I started cooking on my own. I just throw them in the pan after the oil and garlic without boiling them and it works like magic. I have used apple cider vinegar instead of balsamic and Splenda instead of sugar and it tasted just as yummy. The sesame oil is the real game changer. I have found this recipe works great with any veggie. It's new, fun and exciting. Thank you for sharing your dad's recipe!

I've been making this weekly for years! i micro trader joe green beans 4 min, drain the water and add the sauce for another 2 minutes. obviously it's better fried but that's the cheaters version and it works =)

I made this recipe a couple of times as written, and it's pretty good. I'm lazy, so now I just substitute Trader Joe's Island Soyaki for the soy sauce, sugar, and oil. I also leave out the vinegar and just add a squeeze of lime juice after pouring the sauce over the beans. Finally, I typically add some nuts (any kind of nut will work) for some extra crunch. Thanks for the recipe!

A great way to spice up fresh green beans. I'm always looking for something new and delicious. This fit the bill! I did cut the following in half oil and soy sauce and it was still great. I've already made it twice. Oh yeah, I steam the green beans in those new ziploc steamer bags before adding the other stuff and cooking in the pan. Makes it a really quick weeknight veggie.

Delicious! I also used 2 T. soy sauce and half the sesame oil. After I had steamed the green beans, I put them in the frypan with the hot sesame oil and garlic and really browned them. After I poured the sauce in, I cooked off most of the liquid. Then I put the cooked beans in toasted corn tortillas and they were a hit for lunch!

I made these beans for the first time utilizing canned beans. Omission of the steaming process made it even quicker. They turned out awesum. My gal and I devoured them with baked trout. Wonderful. Thanks for the recipe.
Bob

Pam, your dad - and his attempt to re-create his famous side dish: AMAZING! Made to pair with a pork dish and, while the pairing wasn’t perfect, these green beans were! We loved them! So simple, so easy, so good! Added to my favorites! Thank you for sharing this recipe with us!
My 3 year old and 6 year old grandkids loved this! We did too! If you can get a kid to eat a vegetable, it has got to be good!
Amazingly good! Make a huge batch, just for the two of us. The flavours work together so well! Have used both fresh and frozen beans - both work equally well!
This is my favorite way to make fresh green beans. The recipe is perfect the way it is. I always triple the recipe and still no leftovers. 😁

I've been doing this recipe now for years and it doesn't matter if I double or triple the recipe, there is never any leftovers. I don't change, add, substitute, or leave out anything...I make it just like it says and everyone loves it!
Make 2 things of soy sauce, balsamic, sugar mix and put on it the pot with the green beans and all the other fixings
Definitely not a veggie person but this is really good. We doubled the sauce mixture for it and added minced onion, garlic salt, and pepper.

As a southern girl, I've tasted just about every green bean recipe there is. This recipe is by FAR my favorite. The sauce highlights the flavor and gives a little kick without overpowering the beans. They also turn out really pretty and bright. My 9 year old loves them as well. All around win!
I was really not sure of these with the Balsamic Vinegar in the sauce but I have to say it was so easy and very good! Thank you!
